questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Seeing a rainbow (1)/ is a sight (2)/ to behold. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The given sentence contains no error as it simply tells that seeing a rainbow is a glimpse worthy of seeing. Therefore, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

The poor girl slept in the attic, upon a hard straw mattress, (1)/ whilst the bed-chambers of the sisters (2)/ were furnishing with every luxury and elegance. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: Solution: The sentence is in past tense as suggested by ‘slept’ and ‘were’. Therefore, the verb furnish should be in the past tense too. Hence, ‘furnished’ should be written instead of ‘furnishing’. The error is therefore in part 3 of the sentence and option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

My family has always ______ me.
questions.solution: The usage of ‘has’ in the given sentence that the action that started in the past still continues in the present. Therefore, the present perfect tense (**sub + has/have + v3 + object** ) should be used. So the main verb supported should be in its third form, i.e., ‘supported’.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

Life is a jigsaw puzzle that is hard to ______.
questions.solution: The given sentence is in the simple present tense as indicated by the auxiliary verb ‘is’. Therefore, the base form of the verb ‘solve’ should be used. Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Longevity
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are as follows:

Longevity => long life

Affinity => liking for or understanding of something

Durability => having the toughness to exist for long

Clearly, option 3 is closest in meaning to the given word.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Aggravate
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are as follows:

Aggravate => make a problem worse; annoy someone

Decline => reduce

Acquire => obtain, get

Excited => enthusiastic

Irritate => annoy someone

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Yearn
questions.solution: ‘Yearn’ means to want something or crave for it. Therefore, option 1 is the best fit answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Duplicate
questions.solution:
‘Duplicate’ refers to an exact copy of something. Therefore, ‘copy’ is a synonym. ‘Replicate’ means to make an exact copy of something. ‘Alternative’ means a replacement or substitute.

Option 2 best expresses the antonym of the given word.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Prior
questions.solution:
Let’s look at the meanings of the given words:

Prior => previous

Sufficient => enough

Subsequent => next

Satire => mockery

Seductive => tempting and attractive

Clearly, option 2 is the antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Amiable
questions.solution:
Let’s look at the meanings of the given words:

Amiable => friendly

Crabby => irritable

Affable => friendly

Clearly, option 1 is the correct antonym.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/ Phrase.**

Don't put all your eggs in one basket

options.text: To put all your resources in one place
Don't put all your resources in one place

questions.solution: The given phrase means that one should not risk everything all at one time. Therefore, option 2 best states its meaning.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/ Phrase.**

Bite the bullet
questions.solution: The idiom ‘bite the bullet’ means to do something which one finds unpleasant. Thus, option 4 is the correct answer

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

When we saw her last time, she( ran) to catch a bus.
questions.solution: The part stating ‘when we **saw **her last time’ indicates that the action of seeing took place in the past and the action (of her running) they saw went on for some time in the past. Therefore, the past continuous tense should be used here which is in the following form: **Subject + was/were +V1+ ing + Object. **Hence, option 1, ‘was running’ is correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

A strong feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant
questions.solution: *A strong feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant* is called a **premonition**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

A public officer appointed to decide cases in a law court
questions.solution: A public officer appointed to **decide** cases in a law court is known as a judge.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

The country

P: due to the

Q: new Prime Minister

R: is in dire straits
questions.solution: R mentions the state in which the country is. P and Q combine to state the reason. Therefore, RPQ is the correct sequence. Note that the state of a particular thing should come before you mention the reason behind it.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

There is

P: gap between

Q: a huge financial

R: the two families
questions.solution: R should definitely follow P as between indicates that there must be two entities. Q has to be the first part as it states what kind of gap is there. Thus, QPR is the correct sequence.

questions.question: Inhabitants of the Earth have cleared ________ forests to make fields for growing crops.
questions.solution: ‘To clear away’ is a phrasal verb which means to ‘remove’, ‘exhaust’ or ‘finish’. Thus, ‘away’ is the correct adverb that should be used here as the forests have been removed to grow crops.

questions.question: They have moved mountains to make ________ for roads
questions.solution: The phrase ‘to make room’ means to remove things to make space for another. In the given context it means that mountains have been cut through to make roads and cities.

questions.question: They have built huge dams ________ rivers
questions.solution: You build dams ‘across’ rivers, that is, they are built from one side to another. Thus option 3 is correct.

questions.question: Once everyone cheered at the progress that man made in changing his _________
questions.solution: From all the progress mentioned earlier in the passage, it can be understood that man made changes in his surrounding or the *environment*. Option 2 is quite a broad term and man may not make changes in it completely. ‘Ecology’ is a branch of study, and is an unfit for the given blank. Option 3 is inappropriate too.

questions.question: many people are worried by the ___________ that such changes can bring.
questions.solution: One cannot be worried about ‘advantages’, ‘benefits’ or ‘agreements’. ‘Problems’ are something to be worried about, therefore, option 4 is the correct answer.
